q: 1. The minimum length beyond which at least one-third of the negative moment reinforcement should extend beyond the inflection point is
options: 12 times the diameter of the bar
explain: Reinforcement must extend beyond the theoretical cut-off point by a distance equal to the effective depth or 12 times the bar diameter, whichever is greater.

q: 2. When bars of two different diameters are to be spliced the lap length is calculated on the basis of
options: three-fourths diameter of the larger bar
explain: The lap length is governed by the smaller diameter bar because the force to be transferred is limited by the capacity of the smaller bar.

q: 3. The minimum cube strength of concrete used for a prestressed member, is
explain: For prestressed concrete, high-grade concrete is mandatory. 350 kg/cm² (roughly M35) is the typical minimum, though often M40 or higher is used for post-tensioning.

q: 4. The cube strength of the concrete used for pre-stressed member should not be less than
explain: As per IS codes, the minimum grade for post-tensioned work is M30-M35, but in many contexts, 25-30 MPa is cited as the lowest threshold for basic prestressed applications.

q: 5. In post-tensioned pre-stressed concrete beam, the end block zone is the zone between the end of the beam and the section where
options: shape of the cross-section of beam
explain: The end block is the region where concentrated anchorage forces disperse into uniform longitudinal stress across the full section (Saint Venant's Principle).

q: 6. The propagation of a shear crack in a pre-stressed concrete member depends upon
options: shape of the cross-section of beam
explain: The shape of the cross-section (like I-beams) significantly influences the distribution of principal stresses and how shear cracks initiate and propagate.

q: 7. An R.C.C. beam not provided with shear reinforcement may develop cracks in its bottom inclined roughly to the horizontal at
explain: Shear stress (diagonal tension) typically acts at a 45-degree angle to the beam axis, which is where cracks initiate if shear reinforcement is absent.

q: 8. In the zone of R.C.C. beam where stress in less than 5 kg/cm², nominal reinforcement is provided at a pitch of
options: one-half lever arm of the section
one-third lever arm of the section
one and half lever arm of the section
explain: Nominal stirrups are typically spaced at a distance equal to the lever arm (or slightly less) to bridge potential 45-degree cracks.

q: 9. The load stress of a section can be reduced by
options: increasing the total perimeter of bars
replacing larger bars by greater number of small bars
replacing smaller bars by greater number of greater bars
explain: Increasing the total perimeter of the reinforcement (by using more bars) improves the bond and reduces the bond stress between concrete and steel.
